What if blood pressure is too low? (top number 90 or less)

object.label: Shock: from infection (sepsis), bleeding (e.g. ectopic, blood thinner), severe allergy, dehydration, heart problem, or a medicine (opioid, BP tablet). Or a faulty reading.

subject.label: Monitor shows 86/52; patient pale, sweaty, dizzy.

relations.note: What if blood pressure is extremely high? (180/110 or more)

object.label: Untreated/poorly treated high BP, pain, anxiety, missed tablets; rarely a hypertensive emergency.

relations.note: What if the heart rate is very high? (above 130)

object.label: Sepsis, bleeding, dehydration, severe pain, fast abnormal rhythm (AF/SVT), lung clot, fever, thyroid.

relations.note: What if the heart rate is very slow? (40 or below)

object.label: Heart block, beta-blocker/digoxin, very high potassium, hypothermia.

relations.note: What if the patient has a fever? (38.0 °C or more)

object.label: S1: inflamed gallbladder or infected bile ducts (if jaundiced); urine/chest infection. S2: appendicitis, worse if 39+ (possible perforation/abscess).

relations.note: What if the patient is cold? (36.0 °C or less)

object.label: Cold environment, long fasting, older age — or severe sepsis (ominous if with other bad signs).

relations.note: What if oxygen saturation is low? (below 94%)

object.label: Probe error; aspiration (vomit in lungs); chest infection; fluid overload after many boluses; lung clot; too much opioid (slow breathing); collapsed lung areas from pain.

relations.note: What if breathing is very fast? (25 or more)

object.label: Sepsis, acid build-up (DKA, poor circulation), lung problem, pain, anxiety.

relations.note: What if breathing is very slow? (8 or less)

object.label: Too much opioid painkiller; severe brain problem.

relations.note: What if the patient becomes confused?

object.label: Low sugar, low oxygen, sepsis, low BP, opioids, low sodium, alcohol withdrawal, stroke.

relations.note: What if pain gets much worse or the tummy becomes rigid?

object.label: Perforation (burst appendix/gallbladder), ruptured ectopic, twisted ovary, blocked/ischaemic bowel.

subject.label: Pain 9/10 despite strong painkiller; whole tummy hard as a board.

relations.note: What if potassium is high? (above 5.3)

object.label: Faulty (haemolysed) sample; kidney injury; medicines (ACE inhibitors, potassium-sparing water tablets, potassium supplements); acid in blood.

relations.note: What if potassium is low? (below 3.5)
What if sodium is abnormal?

object.label: Water tablets, vomiting replaced by plain water, hormonal causes, heart/liver failure.

relations.note: What if haemoglobin is low?

object.label: Long-term iron deficiency, thalassaemia trait, slow gut bleeding, or acute bleeding (S2 ectopic).

relations.note: What if the white cell count is high?
What if the white cell count is low?

object.label: Overwhelming sepsis, viral illness, medicines, bone-marrow problem.

relations.note: What if creatinine is high?

object.label: Acute kidney injury from dehydration, sepsis, medicines; or long-term kidney disease (compare old result).

relations.note: What if liver tests are abnormal?

object.label: Bile duct blockage (stone), passing stone, inflamed gallbladder, hepatitis, alcohol, medicines.

relations.note: What if bilirubin is high?

object.label: Blocked bile duct; liver disease; red cell breakdown; Gilbert's (if mild alone).

relations.note: What if blood sugar is low? (below 4.0)

object.label: Diabetes medicine while fasting; sepsis; alcohol.

relations.note: What if blood sugar is high? (above 12)

object.label: Infection, stress, missed medicine, steroids, undiagnosed diabetes, DKA.

relations.note: What if the clotting test (INR) is high?

object.label: Liver disease, long bile blockage (vitamin K not absorbed), sepsis, error.

relations.note: What if lactate is raised?

object.label: Organs short of oxygen: sepsis, dehydration, bleeding (rarely: some medicines, liver disease).

relations.note: What if the ECG is abnormal?

object.label: AF triggered by sepsis/dehydration/salts; heart attack; potassium problem.

subject.label: ECG: irregular, no P waves, rate 132 (new AF). Or ST elevation with chest pain.

relations.note: What if the patient is pregnant?

object.label: Normal early pregnancy; ectopic pregnancy (if pain/bleeding); miscarriage.

relations.note: What if pregnancy status is unknown or the patient declines a test?

object.label: Patient choice; privacy concerns; family present.

relations.note: What if the patient is allergic to an antibiotic?

object.label: Mild vs severe allergy (or intolerance like nausea).

subject.label: "Penicillin gave me a rash" / "…made my throat swell".

relations.note: What if an allergic reaction happens after a medicine?

subject.label: Minutes after an antibiotic: hives, swollen lips, wheeze, BP 80/45.

relations.note: What if the patient takes blood thinners?

object.label: Bleeding risk in surgery; clot/stroke risk if stopped.

relations.note: What if the patient has diabetes?

object.label: Fasting may cause low sugar; stress/infection may cause high sugar.

subject.label: "I have type 2 diabetes, on metformin and gliclazide."

relations.note: What if the patient takes steroids, GLP-1 injections or SGLT2 tablets?

object.label: Steroids: needs extra cover. GLP-1: stomach may be full. SGLT2: hidden DKA risk.

relations.note: What if the patient hasn't fasted?
What if fasting status is unknown?

subject.label: Confused/unwell patient can't remember; no relative.

relations.note: What if imaging is inconclusive?
What if a test result doesn't make sense?

object.label: Faulty sample (haemolysis, clumping, drip arm, wrong patient).

subject.label: K 7.1 in a chatty, well man; platelets 40 in a well woman.

relations.note: What if a laboratory result is delayed?
What if a critical result is phoned through?
What if the patient deteriorates?

object.label: Complication (perforation, sepsis, bleeding), wrong diagnosis, medicine reaction.

subject.label: Vital signs trending worse; NEWS2 rising (e.g. 2 → 5).

relations.note: What if the patient becomes septic?

subject.label: Infection + NEWS2 ≥5 or lactate ≥2 or BP ≤100 or confusion.

relations.note: What if the patient refuses surgery?

object.label: Fear, misunderstanding, cost/family concerns, cultural reasons, informed choice.

relations.note: What if the patient cannot understand the consent discussion?

object.label: Language barrier, hearing problem, confusion/no capacity, low health literacy.

relations.note: What if the patient is under 18?

object.label: A minor in most jurisdictions (age of majority and medical-consent rules vary CONTEXT-DEPENDENT — INSTITUTIONAL PROTOCOL / CLINICIAN CONFIRMATION ).

relations.note: What if equipment fails?

subject.label: Gas pump low, suction not working, oximeter not reading.

relations.note: What if documents are missing?
What if the patient deteriorates during transfer?

subject.label: Oxygen falls to 89% in the corridor.

relations.note: What if there's an identity mismatch at theatre?

subject.label: Wristband MR number differs from list.
